title: Christopher Nolan
subtitle: the directed features
blurb: Thirteen features in release order, from a $6,000 debut to The Odyssey — 30 hours and 8 minutes of them, nine of the thirteen running over two hours each.
notes: The filmography's Feature film table has fourteen rows. The fourteenth is Man of Steel (2013), and its Director cell says no: Nolan produced that film and wrote its story, and Zack Snyder directed it. Only a bare director credit puts a film on this list.

Out: the films he produced or executive produced for other directors — Man of Steel, Transcendence, Batman v Superman, both cuts of Justice League, and Sanatorium Under the Sign of the Hourglass. Also out: the four shorts he directed — Tarantella, Larceny, Doodlebug and Quay — which the source keeps in a separate table under its own heading and does not treat as features. Either set can be added if the list would rather have them.

From Wikidata, in hours, for all thirteen — 30 hours 8 minutes in total. Every runtime comes from that one source and the generator refuses to build otherwise, because three of the films' own Wikipedia infoboxes give a different number (The Prestige 130 against 125, The Dark Knight 152 against 153, The Odyssey 173 against 172). Picking whichever is handier per film would produce a total belonging to no source at all.
It starts at Following because the source does.

A footnote on the filmography records a feature called Larry Mahoney that Nolan directed in the mid-1990s; it was scrapped and never released. There is nothing to watch and no runtime to weigh, so it is mentioned here rather than listed above.
Filmography from Wikipedia's Christopher Nolan filmography, read from the enumerated tables and not from its prose; runtimes from Wikidata (P2047), gated on a matching release year.

sections.title: Before the franchise
sections.intro: Following was made for $6,000 and runs 70 minutes, the shortest thing here by a distance. Memento came from a short story his brother Jonathan wrote. Insomnia, a remake of a Norwegian film, was his first for Warner Bros. — and the only one of the thirteen he did not write.

items.note: Also his own cinematographer and editor · Made for $6,000
Adapted from Memento Mori, a short story by Jonathan Nolan
A remake of the 1997 Norwegian film of the same name · The only one of the thirteen he did not write

sections.title: The Batman years
sections.intro: Five films in seven years: a Batman trilogy, with The Prestige and Inception made between its instalments. From The Prestige onward he produces everything he directs, and Warner Bros. is on all five — though The Prestige went out through Buena Vista in the United States.

items.note: Adapted from The Prestige, a novel by Christopher Priest

sections.title: Three originals in a row
sections.intro: No franchise behind any of the three, and all three made at the scale the Batman films had bought him. Interstellar, at 169 minutes, was the longest he had made to that point; Dunkirk, at 106, is still the shortest since his debut.

sections.title: Universal
sections.intro: Two films for Universal, after eighteen years in which Warner Bros. was on the release of every film he directed. They are also the two longest he has made: 180 minutes and 172.

items.note: Adapted from American Prometheus, a biography by Kai Bird and Martin J. Sherwin · His longest feature
